title: bias_core cold-start branch selection: transient supply ramp from 0 V across the full PVT matrix
claim: Issue #19 -- NOT a spec claim (spec/target-spec.md does not exist yet, spec/porting-plan.md Sec4 item 4). Substantiates that bias_core reaches its intended operating branch (VREF ~1.25 V, ~1 uA quiescent draw, BIAS_OK asserted) from a physical 0 V cold start at every point of the full 45-point PVT matrix -- i.e. that the on-die startup kick reliably breaks the degenerate zero-current state without any solver assistance. This is the branch-selection counterpart to sim/bias-core-smoke/, whose cold `.op` cannot make that claim: a `.op` has no initial state, so which branch it lands on is chosen by ngspice's gmin-stepping continuation rather than by the circuit. See sim/bias-core-op-branch/ for the measured evidence that the two spurious `.op` points in sim/bias-core-smoke/records/20260825-214036-a9cac4b.md are solver artifacts, not a second stable state.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

measurements.name: vref
measurements.note: Settled reference output at t=tstop, open circuit. Same harness-liveness window as sim/bias-core-smoke/'s own vref bound (deliberately a few hundred mV around design/bias_core.md's 1.2477-1.2574 V spot check), NOT a spec claim. The point of this experiment is WHICH branch is reached, not the exact value.

measurements.name: vref_settled
measurements.note: Settling guard: VREF must move less than 1 mV over the last 100 output steps (1 ms of the 10 ms window). Without this, a run that was still ramping at t=tstop could report an in-band VREF it had not actually settled to. nlast-100 is well past the 100 us supply ramp at every corner.

measurements.name: ibias
measurements.note: IBIAS is open-circuit (no load in this testbench), so per design/bias_core.md's own compliance note it rails toward VDD. Window covers the full 2.97-3.63 V supply range with margin, matching sim/bias-core-smoke/'s bound.

measurements.name: bias_ok
measurements.note: BIAS_OK active-high settle flag; must read rail-high once the core is up. In THIS experiment that is a real startup assertion, not just a liveness bound: BIAS_OK low at the end of a 0 V-cold-start ramp would mean the on-die kick failed to clear the degenerate zero-current state at that corner.

measurements.name: isup
measurements.note: Total quiescent supply current at t=tstop. Same generous harness bound as sim/bias-core-smoke/. The lower bound also rejects the degenerate zero-current state, and the sign rejects the non-physical `.op` artifact this experiment exists to displace (that artifact reports a NEGATIVE supply current, i.e. the circuit sourcing milliamps into its own only energy source).

spread_checks.note: Same corner-blindness guard as sim/bias-core-smoke/: if every corner returns the same settled vref, the .lib/.temp injection is not taking effect.

notes: Analyses list carries one non-analysis control line (`let nlast = length(v(vref))-1`). corner-run.py splices `deck.analyses` verbatim into the .control block ahead of the `let meas_* = <expr>` lines, so this is the supported way to define a helper vector the measurement expressions index against; nutmeg has no `last()` accessor.

Ramp rate is fixed at 'vsup'/'tramp' = ~30 kV/s (100 us 0->3.3 V) for every corner. That is one point on the supply-ramp-rate axis, not coverage of it -- root CLAUDE.md's ramp-rate matrix requirement belongs to the POR block's own testbenches (spec/porting-plan.md Sec3), not to this bias-core branch-selection check. sim/bias-core-op-branch/ additionally re-runs the failing `.op` supply points at a second, 1000x slower ramp, to confirm the branch reached does not depend on ramp rate at the points that matter here.

`uic` is what makes this a cold start: it skips the initial operating-point solve entirely and integrates forward from all-zero initial conditions. Without `uic`, ngspice would compute a `.op` at t=0 first, reintroducing exactly the solver-chosen initial guess this experiment exists to avoid.
